title: 2.2.2 Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.)
description: Field pea: uses, rotation, planting, protection and harvesting

questions.question: What is the botanical name of field pea?
For what purpose is field pea produced?
Which nutrient is field pea seed notably rich in?
Besides human food, what other important role does field pea play?
options: It is an important source of animal feed
It is an important source of firewood
It is an important source of industrial oil
It is an important source of building material
questions.correctAnswer: It is an important source of animal feed

questions.question: How is field pea commonly planted?
options: As a mono crop or mixed with faba bean
Only as a mono crop far from other crops
questions.correctAnswer: As a mono crop or mixed with faba bean

questions.question: With which crops is field pea usually grown in rotation?
options: Cereals such as teff, wheat and barley
Cereals such as maize and sorghum only
Root crops such as potato and enset
Fibre crops such as cotton and sesame
questions.correctAnswer: Cereals such as teff, wheat and barley

questions.question: At what altitude range does field pea grow well?
options: $2200$ to $2600$ m above sea level only

questions.question: Which methods are used to plant field pea?
What spacing is used between rows when field pea is planted in rows?
What spacing is used between plants of field pea?
Which insect pests reduce the productivity of field pea?
options: Maize stalk borer and army worm

questions.question: Besides insect pests, which other problems affect field pea productivity?
When should manual weeding of field pea start?
Which methods are combined in the integrated control of field pea weeds, pests and diseases?
options: Manual weeding, crop rotation and chemical methods
questions.correctAnswer: Manual weeding, crop rotation and chemical methods

questions.question: What is the indicator that field pea pods are ready for harvest?
options: The pod is mature and the seeds are sufficiently hard
The pod is still green and the seeds are soft
The leaves are still bright green and wet
questions.correctAnswer: The pod is mature and the seeds are sufficiently hard

questions.question: What happens when field pea harvesting is delayed?
options: Seeds are lost from the pods through shattering
The pods become heavier and do not break
The seeds turn into animal feed on the plant
The plants start to produce a second crop
questions.correctAnswer: Seeds are lost from the pods through shattering

questions.question: What is the average national yield of field pea in Ethiopia?
The national average field pea yield of $14$ quintals per hectare equals how many tonnes per hectare?
Which group of Ethiopian field crops includes field pea?
How does soil cultivation for field pea generally compare with that for cereals?
options: It is generally minimal; the soil is cultivated once or direct planting is done
It is always heavier than that of cereals
It is done only after harvesting the cereal
questions.correctAnswer: It is generally minimal; the soil is cultivated once or direct planting is done

questions.question: How does field pea contribute to soil nitrogen?
options: It fixes atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules, leaving nitrogen for later crops
It takes up nitrogen from the soil and stores it in the pods
It prevents nitrogen from entering the field
It changes nitrogen into a form that plants cannot use
questions.correctAnswer: It fixes atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules, leaving nitrogen for later crops

questions.question: In Ethiopia, field pea and other pulses are mostly produced in which way regarding mineral fertilizer?
options: With the highest mineral fertilizer rate of all crops
With mineral fertilizer applied at flowering only
With mineral fertilizer applied by broadcasting in dry season
